task:
A named Dict that matches nothing turns into a list in as_dict(), and ParseResults does not survive pickling exactly. Fix both.

Take parser1 = pp.Dict(pp.ZeroOrMore(pp.Group(pp.Word(pp.alphas) + pp.Word(pp.alphas)))) and parser2 = parser1.copy()('fubar').

These already work and must keep working: parser1.parse_string('foo bar').as_dict() gives {'foo': 'bar'}, parser2.parse_string('foo bar').as_dict() gives {'fubar': {'foo': 'bar'}}, and parser1.parse_string('').as_dict() gives {}.

This one is wrong: parser2.parse_string('').as_dict() gives {'fubar': []}. It must give {'fubar': {}}. The result from Dict must keep its dict meaning even when it has no entries.

Pickling must keep the whole state of a ParseResults, in every pickle protocol from 0 to pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL. Take result = pp.make_html_tags('BODY')[0].parse_string("<BODY BGCOLOR='#00FFBB' FGCOLOR=black>", parse_all=True) and newresult = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(result, protocol)). For every name in pp.ParseResults.__slots__ except '_parent', getattr(result, name) must equal getattr(newresult, name). Today this raises AttributeError or reports a mismatch. Any new state you add must meet the same rule, and any slot that no longer serves a purpose should go. newresult.dump() must equal result.dump().

For that check to hold, ParseResults values must compare with ==. Two ParseResults are equal when they have the same type, the same results name, the same as_list() and the same as_dict(). An object equals itself.

Dict must not fail when the first token of one of its groups is a nested ParseResults, because such a value cannot be a dict key. Parsing must succeed, and that group simply gets no key.

Everything else must keep working.
